title: The System of Parks: a Forest Engineer in the Cities of Four Continents
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Savoyard, the Polytechnique, and the Forest School

stops.name: Aix-les-Bains, birth in a department one year old
stops.date_confidence: attested; en.wikipedia and the Cite de l'architecture authority biography agree on the day and the place
stops.campa: Jean-Claude Nicolas Forestier is born at Aix-les-Bains on the ninth of January, in a Savoie annexed to France barely a year before. The spa town lives on its waters and on the visitors the waters bring. The lake lies below and the Bauges rise behind. The ground between them is already a public amenity: laid out for walking, prescribed by physicians, paid for by strangers who come to take the cure. The first landscape he knows well is one arranged for the use of people who do not live in it.
suggested_refs: The thermal establishment and lakeside promenades of Aix-les-Bains under the Second Empire
sources: Cite de l'architecture, portraits d'architectes, forje.php

stops.name: Ecole polytechnique, Paris: the engineer's formation
stops.date_confidence: year attested (en.wikipedia; es.wikipedia gives 1880/1882); month and day unknown, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: At nineteen he enters the Ecole polytechnique, the school that supplies France with its engineers, its artillery officers, and its administrators. He learns surveying, hydraulics, mathematics, the drawing of ground as a set of measurable quantities. Nothing in the curriculum concerns gardens. What it gives him is the habit of thinking at the scale of a territory and of costing whatever he proposes, and that habit will separate him for the rest of his life from the horticulturists he works beside. He leaves about 1882 and takes courses at the Ecole libre des sciences politiques instead.
suggested_refs: A brief attachment to the Ministry of Finance is reported by one biographer, Guerin, and appears in no other source; the Cite de l'architecture omits it entirely

stops.name: Ecole forestiere de Nancy, the change of career
stops.date_confidence: attested that he trained here to 1885 (es.wikipedia, en.wikipedia, Cite de l'architecture); the start year is es.wikipedia's 1883/1885 range, month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He turns from finance to trees. At the forest school of Nancy he studies botany, hydraulics, silviculture, and the management of a territory as a renewable stock, and leaves as a trainee garde general of the Eaux et Forets. The school trains men to read a forest as a hundred-year account book and to plant for successors they will never meet. Forestier will apply the same accounting to cities, where the stock to be secured before it vanishes is not timber but open ground, and where the price rises every year the purchase is put off. The school stands on a street named for Lyautey.
suggested_refs: The Ecole nationale des eaux et forets, Nancy, today AgroParisTech, rue Lyautey

stops.name: Argeles-Gazost, the first posting
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; es.wikipedia names Argeles among three 1885-1887 postings but the locality is ambiguous, Argeles-Gazost in the Hautes-Pyrenees being the reading that fits a Water-and-Forests district; Argeles-sur-Mer is the other candidate
stops.campa: His first posting sends him into the Pyrenees, to the Water and Forests district of Argeles. He is twenty-four. He walks cutting rights and grazing disputes, marks trees, measures torrents, and learns the part of the work no school teaches: a landscape is held by the people who use it, and any plan for it is a negotiation with them before it is a drawing. Which Argeles the record means is disputed. Argeles-Gazost in the Hautes-Pyrenees fits a Water-and-Forests district; Argeles-sur-Mer on the Mediterranean cannot be ruled out.
suggested_refs: Records of the Eaux et Forets district of Argeles-Gazost, Hautes-Pyrenees, 1885
sources: dossier account of the Guerin career sequence, not independently confirmed

stops.name: Annecy, the alpine apprenticeship
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; es.wikipedia gives 'Argeles, Annecy y Sallanches' across 1885-1887 without dating the individual postings, so the year here orders the sequence
stops.campa: Transferred to Annecy, he serves in the alpine country of his own childhood, and then at Sallanches at the foot of Mont Blanc in the last months before Paris. Two years, three postings, no drawing from any of them survives. Then the City of Paris takes him into the Service des Promenades et Plantations, and the man trained to husband forests across a century begins a municipal career that will run forty years and end only when he dies. He never returns to the Eaux et Forets.
suggested_refs: The third posting, Sallanches, dropped from most summaries of his career but present in the Spanish chronology
sources: dossier account of the Guerin career sequence

segments.name: The Service des Promenades et Plantations

stops.name: Bois de Vincennes, entry into the City of Paris
stops.date_confidence: year attested (es.wikipedia, en.wikipedia); the 1890 cycle track in the same wood is single-source and no works order has been found
stops.campa: He enters the Service des Promenades et Plantations as an assistant conservator of the Bois de Vincennes, the eastern wood the Second Empire handed to the city as a working park. He will serve this administration for four decades and never head it. Here he holds ground rather than invents it: drainage, plantations, the traffic of a whole quarter's Sundays. A Spanish chronology credits the first cycling track in the Bois to works under his charge in 1890. No works order has been found, and the English record mentions no track anywhere.
suggested_refs: Registers of the Service des Promenades et Plantations for the Bois de Vincennes, 1887-1898

stops.name: Avenue de Breteuil, the revision that is rejected
stops.date_confidence: the 1898 western-sector work is attested by en.wikipedia; the Formige revision and its rejection on cost come from the dossier's account of Guerin and are reconstruction
stops.campa: Working the western sector of the Promenades de Paris, he takes Jean-Camille Formige's planting scheme for the Avenue de Breteuil and rewrites it. His version costs more. The city rejects it and builds Formige's. It is an early demonstration of his standing inside the house that employs him: the conservator proposes, the administration decides, and the designs that carry his own signature will more often be built abroad than in the city he serves. He keeps proposing. The Bois de Boulogne comes into his charge in the same years.
suggested_refs: Jean-Camille Formige's executed planting design for the Avenue de Breteuil
sources: dossier account of the Guerin biography

stops.name: Bagatelle, the estate bought for the city
stops.date_confidence: the Bois de Boulogne is attested among his Paris projects (en.wikipedia); the 1904-1910 Bagatelle acquisition campaign and rose garden detail come from the dossier; year within the span
stops.campa: He drives the campaign for the city to buy Bagatelle, the small eighteenth-century estate inside the Bois de Boulogne, then privately held and for sale. Paris takes it. It is the one Paris commission he is left alone to finish. Forestier restores the grounds and plants a rose garden as a trial field, laying the beds out so that varieties can be judged one against another, and from 1907 the garden holds an international competition for new roses that will outlive him by a century.
suggested_refs: The Concours international de roses nouvelles de Bagatelle, held annually from 1907
sources: dossier detail on the Bagatelle acquisition

stops.name: Paris, Grandes villes et systemes de parcs
stops.date_confidence: contradiction left open: the text is dated December 1905 with a 1906 Hachette printing per digitized catalogue copies, while es.wikipedia and the current Editions Norma page both give 1908; both datings circulate and neither is adopted here
stops.campa: He publishes the book that makes him an urbanist rather than a gardener. Its argument is administrative before it is aesthetic: a hierarchy of great reserves, suburban parks, neighbourhood gardens, and planted promenades, land to be reserved while it is still cheap, distribution as important as total surface. In the same years he campaigns for the obsolete ring of Paris fortifications to be kept as open ground for the city. The ring is built over. The book goes on being reprinted, and the year of its first edition is still disputed.
stops.quote: Le plan de ville est insuffisant s'il n'est pas complete par un programme d'ensemble et un plan special des espaces libres interieurs et exterieurs, pour le present et pour l'avenir, - par un systeme de parcs
stops.quote_source: Grandes villes et systemes de parcs, p. 56 of the 1997 Norma critical edition (Leclerc and Tarrago), as quoted with page citation on fr.wikipedia; the 1997 book itself was not obtained
suggested_refs: Grandes villes et systemes de parcs, critical edition, ed. B. Leclerc and S. Tarrago, Paris: Norma, 1997
sources: dossier account of the Hachette catalogue and digitized copies

stops.name: Musee social, the hygiene section
stops.date_confidence: attested by the dossier for the Musee social section; the 1911 founding of the Societe francaise des architectes urbanistes is attested by es.wikipedia and mentioned here out of its own year
stops.campa: He becomes a founding participant in the Urban and Rural Hygiene section of the Musee social, the reformist institute where French urbanism is being assembled out of mortality statistics, housing law, and the English garden-city literature. The forest officer has turned lobbyist. The case he presses in committee is the one he made in print: open space is infrastructure, and infrastructure is bought early or not at all. Three years later he is among the founders of the Societe francaise des architectes urbanistes.
stops.quote: Il y a non seulement a calculer quelle doit etre la surface moyenne d'espaces libres a prevoir pour une population determinee, il faut aussi se preoccuper de leur plus efficace distribution et de leur uniforme repartition
stops.quote_source: Grandes villes et systemes de parcs, p. 59 of the 1997 Norma critical edition, as quoted with page citation on fr.wikipedia; original not independently accessed
suggested_refs: The Section d'hygiene urbaine et rurale of the Musee social, Paris

stops.name: Giverny, the report on Monet's garden
stops.date_confidence: the 1908 illustrated report is attested by the dossier; month unknown, set within the growing season to order the sequence
stops.campa: He goes down the Seine to Giverny and publishes an illustrated report on Claude Monet's garden, treating it as composition rather than as a painter's private eccentricity. The massed colour, the water, the planted bridge: he reads the borders as a made thing with rules that can be stated, and looks at the beds the way Nancy taught him to look at a forest stand, for structure and for succession. The colour lessons turn up later in Seville. Monet is sixty-eight and still working.
suggested_refs: Forestier's 1908 illustrated report on the garden of Claude Monet at Giverny
sources: dossier account of the published 1908 report

segments.name: Andalusia, and the Reserves of Morocco

stops.name: Parque de Maria Luisa, Seville: the palace gardens opened to the city
stops.date_confidence: engagement year attested (en.wikipedia, 'Parque de Maria Luisa'); month and day defaulted; note that es.wikipedia dates the park's inauguration 1914 while the exposition it was made for did not open until 1929
stops.campa: Seville engages him to turn the grounds of the old San Telmo palace, given to the city by the Duchess of Montpensier, into a public park for a Hispano-American exposition still years from opening. He cuts shaded axes through the standing trees, sets tiled pools and glorietas in the enclosures between them, and works the vocabulary of Andalusian and Hispano-Moorish gardens without copying any single one. In 1913 he conceives the Fountain of the Lions, carved afterwards by Manuel Delgado Brackembury. The park opens in 1914. The exposition waits until 1929.
suggested_refs: The Fountain of the Lions, Parque de Maria Luisa, sculpted by Manuel Delgado Brackembury

stops.name: Casa del Rey Moro, Ronda: the terraces above the Tajo
stops.date_confidence: year attested (en.wikipedia); month and day unknown, defaulted
stops.campa: The Duchess of Parcent brings him to Ronda, to the Casa del Rey Moro on the lip of the Tajo gorge. The site is nearly vertical. He terraces it in three levels, hangs pergolas and water channels off the rock, and plants myrtle, oleander, cypress and cedar so that the descent reads as a sequence of rooms rather than as a slope. The garden is the fullest surviving example of the Mediterranean manner he is working out in these Spanish years. Below the last terrace, the water mine cut in the Middle Ages still drops through the cliff to the river.
suggested_refs: The medieval water mine of the Casa del Rey Moro, descending inside the cliff to the Guadalevin

stops.name: Rabat, the report on the reserves
stops.date_confidence: the 1913 Lyautey commission is attested (en.wikipedia); the seventy-page report and its December date come from the dossier's citation of the Rapport des reserves; the Rabat Jardin d'Essais of about seventeen hectares, mentioned here, is reconstruction
stops.campa: Resident-General Hubert Lyautey, governing a protectorate two years old and determined that its cities not be wrecked the way Algiers was, asks Forestier to come and look. He delivers a report of some seventy pages proposing reserves to be constituted inside and around the capital cities of Morocco: Rabat, Fez, Meknes, Marrakesh, the ground to be taken before speculation takes it. He tells Lyautey to engage Henri Prost to carry the work, and Prost is engaged. A trial garden of some seventeen hectares follows at Rabat the next year.
suggested_refs: Rapport des reserves a constituer au dedans et aux abords des villes capitales du Maroc, December 1913

stops.name: The Menara, Marrakesh: olive and palm as reservation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; es.wikipedia confirms a 1913 Marrakech anteproyecto without landmark-level detail, and what was proposed cannot be separated from what was decreed in any source reachable here
stops.campa: His Marrakesh proposals treat the Menara and the Agdal, the old sultanic olive groves with their still basins of water, as reservations to be protected in law, together with the palm grove and the market gardens that feed the city. These are working landscapes rather than picturesque relics, and their survival depends on somebody holding title before the town arrives. Which of these proposals was ever decreed, and which stayed on paper, is not recoverable from the sources reachable here.
suggested_refs: The Menara basin and olive grove, and the Agdal gardens, Marrakesh

stops.name: Montjuic, Barcelona: the hill taken in hand
stops.date_confidence: 1915 arrival attested by Vincent Casals Costa in Scripta Nova 296(2), correcting the 1916 date carried in secondary summaries; en.wikipedia gives no date for Montjuic at all; month defaulted to order the sequence
stops.campa: Francesc Cambo of the Lliga Regionalista brings him to Barcelona to landscape Montjuic, the bare hill over the port, for an exhibition of electrical industries that will eventually become the world's fair of 1929. The hill is quarried, dry, and steep. He plans it as a system of terraces, stairs, and water descending the slope, and takes on a young Catalan collaborator, Nicolau Maria Rubio i Tuduri, who will carry the Barcelona work for decades after Forestier has gone. The program grows for eight years.
suggested_refs: Vincent Casals Costa, Scripta Nova 296(2), on Forestier's arrival in Barcelona in 1915

stops.name: Pedralbes, the garden city that is not bought
stops.date_confidence: the 1916 Pedralbes park start is attested by en.wikipedia; the thousand-hectare scale and the collapse mechanism come from the dossier and Casals Costa, who dates Cambo's move to a Madrid ministry to 1918
stops.campa: The Montjuic commission opens into something far larger: a park and extension scheme at Pedralbes on the city's upper edge, imagined at over a thousand hectares. It requires land, and the land requires Eusebi Guell, who declines to sell. Then Cambo leaves Barcelona city politics in 1918 to take the Ministry of Public Works in Madrid, and the initiative loses the only man who could have forced it through. The drawings survive. The acquisition never happens. Barcelona keeps the hill and loses the mountain.
suggested_refs: The Pedralbes park and extension drawings, Barcelona, c. 1916-1922

stops.name: Palacio de Liria, Madrid: a private commission
stops.date_confidence: year attested (en.wikipedia); month defaulted; how much of the present gardens is his cannot be established, the palace having burned in the civil war and been rebuilt
stops.campa: In Madrid he redesigns the gardens of the Palacio de Liria for the house of Alba, one of the private commissions that pay for the public ones. Parterres, clipped hedging, water on axis with the palace front, box and cypress carrying the design through a Madrid summer. The gardens are altered afterwards, the palace burns in the civil war and is rebuilt, and what a visitor walks through today is a reconstruction of a reconstruction. How much of the plan under it is Forestier's is a question the record does not answer.
suggested_refs: The gardens of the Palacio de Liria, Madrid, reconstructed after the civil war

stops.name: Jardins de Laribal, the terraces on the slope
stops.date_confidence: attested as completed by 1922 (en.wikipedia); the Teatre Grec and Umbracle settings, mentioned here, are reconstruction from the dossier, as is the exact division of hands with Rubio i Tuduri
stops.campa: On the Montjuic slope the Laribal gardens take their finished form, worked out with Rubio i Tuduri: stepped walks under pergolas, water running in tiled channels down the length of the stair, small pools at the landings, brick and glazed ceramic used as he learned to use them in Andalusia. The hill he was called to for a fair of electrical machinery has become the largest work of his life. The Greek Theatre and the Umbracle belong to the same program, and from the terraces of Miramar the whole port lies open below.
suggested_refs: The Jardins de Laribal, Jardins de Miramar, and Teatre Grec, Montjuic

stops.name: Beziers, the garden for Joseph Guy
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the dossier gives the client, the town, and the year, and nothing else; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He designs a private garden at Beziers for Joseph Guy, in the last year of the war, while the reconstruction of the ruined north is already being argued about. The private commissions run through his whole career in a quieter register than the capitals. They are how a municipal officer on a city salary keeps a practice going, and they are where he works at a size he controls entirely. This one is later dispersed and partly restored. What survives of it in the record is a name, a town, a year.
suggested_refs: The Joseph Guy garden at Beziers, dispersed and partly restored

stops.name: Cite internationale universitaire, the park of a garden city
stops.date_confidence: attested by the dossier and by the CIUP's own history page for the 1921 foundation; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: With the architect Lucien Bechmann he takes charge of the park for the new Cite internationale universitaire, raised on the old fortification belt at the southern edge of Paris, the very ground he had argued for fifteen years earlier should be kept open. It is a garden city in miniature: residence halls for the students of many nations set in lawn, walks and sports grounds between them, housing and open space treated as one problem. The campus names an avenue for its patron David David-Weill. Nothing in it carries Forestier's name.
suggested_refs: ciup.fr, '1921: naissance d'une utopie', which names no Forestier memorial on the campus

stops.name: Cours-la-Reine, the gardens of the 1925 Exposition
stops.date_confidence: attested that he directed or inspected the exposition's garden component (en.wikipedia); month and day defaulted to the exposition year
stops.campa: He is put in charge of the garden component of the Exposition internationale des arts decoratifs et industriels modernes, staged on the Cours-la-Reine and the ground about the Grand Palais. The exhibition that will give Art Deco its name treats gardens as designed objects among other designed objects. The assignment is once again an inspectorate: he judges and arranges what other people have planted. What he made of that, after twenty years of arguing that open space is a municipal utility, is not on record.
suggested_refs: The garden section of the Exposition internationale des arts decoratifs et industriels modernes, Paris 1925

segments.name: Buenos Aires: the City Turned Toward Its River

stops.name: Estacion Constitucion, arrival with a month to work
stops.date_confidence: arrival date and the month-long stay come from the dossier; the advisory role to the Comision de Estetica Edilicia and the Constitucion-to-Libertador axis are confirmed on the Observatorio AMBA page
stops.campa: He lands in Buenos Aires on the twelfth of November and has about a month. The Comision de Estetica Edilicia wants a plan. The city has passed two million people and turned its back on the river it was founded on. His collaborator is Carlos Leon Thays, son of the Carlos Thays whose two decades of planting made the park system he is now asked to extend. What he proposes is the hierarchy of his book: great reserves, district parks, planted avenues, tied together by a coastal system running from Constitucion station north to the Avenida del Libertador.
suggested_refs: Observatorio AMBA, Proyecto de espacios libres 1925, Forestier
sources: observatorioamba.org, 1925 Proyecto Organico, proyecto de espacios libres

stops.name: Costanera Sur, ten kilometres of made ground
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia lists Avenida Costera de Buenos Aires, 1924; the width and the dredged-fill construction come from the dossier; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The centrepiece is the river. He proposes some ten kilometres of made coast, two to three hundred metres wide, built out of fill dredged from the port works, planted and given over to promenade, so that a city which has spent a century facing inland is turned around to look at the Plata. Parts of it are built. Decades later, and by nobody's plan, the fill behind the seawall silts up, floods, grows willows and reeds, and becomes a nature reserve inside the capital.
suggested_refs: The Costanera Sur seawall and the ecological reserve that formed behind it

stops.name: Plaza San Martin, the design that is not his
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the dossier corrects a widespread misattribution, the connection being advisory only, and no signed Forestier drawing for the plaza has surfaced; month set to order the sequence within the 1923-1925 consultancy
stops.campa: His plan reaches the Retiro slope and the Plaza San Martin, the hinge between the old city and the northern parks. He advises on the corridor and no more. A legend grows afterwards that he designed the plaza; the city's own histories give that design to Carlos Thays, and the Retiro extension to Thays's son and to municipal works of the nineteen-thirties. No drawing signed by Forestier for the plaza has ever surfaced. Benito Carrasco, who ran Parks and Gardens and had a rival scheme of his own, had opposed hiring a foreigner at all.
suggested_refs: turismo.buenosaires.gob.ar history of Plaza San Martin, crediting Carlos Thays; not fetched directly in this pass
sources: dossier account of the Observatorio Metropolitano breakdown of the 1925 Plan Noel

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the plan published and shelved
stops.date_confidence: the 1925 publication of the Comision de Estetica Edilicia's Proyecto Organico with his open-space sections is attested; della Paolera's competing 1925 plan is noted in QUEUE.md and is not a Forestier source
stops.campa: The Comision de Estetica Edilicia publishes its Proyecto Organico para la urbanizacion del municipio, the Plan Noel, with his open-space and coastal sections inside it. The volume goes to the city legislature library and largely stays there. In the same year Carlos Maria della Paolera comes back from France with a competing plan of his own, and the two circulate together. He also draws a scheme for Ostende, the small resort on the province's Atlantic coast, which most later accounts mistake for Ostend in Belgium.
suggested_refs: Proyecto Organico para la urbanizacion del municipio, Buenos Aires 1925, held at the city legislature library
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Jean-Claude Nicolas Forestier' (wikitext, which reads Ostende, Buenos Aires)

stops.name: Parque 3 de Febrero, the Andalusian courtyard built without him
stops.date_confidence: decree date and the 13 October 1929 opening, with the reported cost, come from the dossier's account of the municipal chronology; Forestier was in France for both and is not recorded as returning to Buenos Aires
stops.campa: A municipal decree of the twenty-second of February orders the Spanish garden at the Palermo entrance to Parque 3 de Febrero built according to Forestier's project. The Patio Andaluz opens on the thirteenth of October at a reported cost of 35,457 pesos moneda nacional: tiled benches, a central basin, clipped hedging, the Andalusian vocabulary he worked out in Seville and Ronda set down inside a park Carlos Thays spent twenty years enlarging. Forestier is in France. He never sees it.
suggested_refs: The Patio or Glorieta Andaluza, Parque 3 de Febrero, decreed 22 February 1929 and opened 13 October 1929
sources: dossier account of the municipal chronology

stops.name: Castillo de la Punta, the first Cuban commission
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the dossier alone reports the Menocal invitation and this 1918 work, and no Cuban archive was reachable in this pass to confirm it; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: President Mario Garcia Menocal invites him to Havana to design the grounds about the Castillo de San Salvador de la Punta, the sixteenth-century fort at the harbour mouth. It is his first Cuban work and the one nobody cites, seven years before the commission that will make his name on the island. Havana in 1918 is rich on wartime sugar. The whole episode rests on a single secondary account; no Cuban archive was reachable to confirm it, and what he drew there, if he drew anything, is unknown.
suggested_refs: The Castillo de San Salvador de la Punta and its grounds at the mouth of Havana harbour

stops.name: Havana, called back by the Secretary of Public Works
stops.date_confidence: the 1925 Cespedes commission under Machado is attested (en.wikipedia); month defaulted; the same source's claim that he 'moved to Havana for a five-year collaboration' is contradicted by the dossier's account of Hartman, which describes three separate visits with much of the work done from Paris, and that conflict is left open
stops.campa: Carlos Miguel de Cespedes, Secretary of Public Works under the new president Gerardo Machado, brings him back at sixty-four to lay out a plan for the whole city. The commission runs to 1929 and is the largest of his life. Machado's government will end in blood and flight, and the avenues will be built anyway. The books say he moved to Havana for five years. The working record shows three separate visits, a Franco-Cuban team, and drawings worked up in Paris and crossing the Atlantic by diplomatic pouch.
suggested_refs: Joseph R. Hartman's scholarship on Forestier in Havana, reached only through the dossier in this pass
sources: dossier account citing Hartman and Guerin

stops.name: El Capitolio, the gardens of the new capitol
stops.date_confidence: the Capitolio gardens and the master plan are attested for 1925-1929 (en.wikipedia); the year here orders the sequence and the month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: He designs the gardens framing the new Capitolio, the domed capitol rising at the edge of the old walled town, and sets them as the pivot of a system: the Prado running north to the sea, the Paseo de Carlos III west, the Parque de la Fraternidad south, the whole tied by planted avenues into a plan a citizen can read on foot. Public works and public theft run together in Machado's Havana, and the gardens go up fast. Royal palms, laurels, tiled walks, benches placed in shade rather than in view.
suggested_refs: El Capitolio, Havana, and its surrounding gardens

stops.name: Paseo del Prado, the promenade rebuilt
stops.date_confidence: the 1928 Prado redesign comes from the dossier; en.wikipedia does not itemise it; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The Prado, the promenade laid out in the eighteenth century between the walled town and the sea, is rebuilt by his team in 1928, at the height of the Havana commission: new terrazzo paving in pattern, marble benches, bronze lions at the ends, the double file of laurels kept and the whole given the character of a room without a roof. It has never once stopped being used for what it was made for. A century afterwards taxi drivers park along it and schoolchildren play under the same trees.
suggested_refs: OnCuba News, 'Jean-Claude Forestier: the Frenchman who helped reshape Havana', 12 April 2021

stops.name: Parque de la Fraternidad, the ceiba and the twenty-eight soils
stops.date_confidence: the 1928 renaming for the Sixth Pan-American Conference and the ceiba planted in soil from twenty-eight countries are attested by en.wikipedia's article on the park, which does not name Forestier; his authorship of the layout comes from es.wikipedia and the dossier and is not independently confirmed
stops.campa: The old Campo de Marte, remade in his plan as the southern anchor of the Capitolio's gardens, is renamed Parque de la Fraternidad Americana for the Sixth Pan-American Conference. At its centre a ceiba is planted in soil carried from twenty-eight American countries. The park's own record of that ceremony does not mention Forestier at all; his authorship of the layout comes from elsewhere, and the two accounts have never been set side by side and reconciled.
suggested_refs: The ceiba of the Parque de la Fraternidad, planted 1928 in soil from twenty-eight American republics

stops.name: Mexico City, the lectures and the earthquake
stops.date_confidence: the visit of 23 September to 9 October 1928 at Quevedo's invitation, and the earthquake on his final night, come from the dossier and were not independently confirmed in this pass
stops.campa: The forest engineer Miguel Angel de Quevedo, who has spent his life planting trees against the erosion of the Valley of Mexico, invites him across. Quevedo's campaign, forests as a condition of a habitable capital, is the argument Forestier has been making about parks since 1906, arrived at from the other end. He stays from the twenty-third of September to the ninth of October, lecturing and consulting. It is the furthest west he ever travels. On his last night in the city a strong earthquake strikes.
suggested_refs: Miguel Angel de Quevedo's reforestation campaign in the Valley of Mexico

stops.name: Loma de los Catalanes, the civic centre proposed
stops.date_confidence: the proposal is attested within the 1925-1929 Havana plan; the 1950s execution is attested by OnCuba News, 12 April 2021, correcting the common claim that the scheme was never realised; month and day defaulted, and the coordinate is the Jose Marti Memorial
stops.campa: The Havana plan proposes moving the civic centre out of the crowded old town to the Loma de los Catalanes, the low hill to the southwest, joined to the historic city by new avenues. Nothing is built there in his lifetime. Machado falls, and the drawings go into a drawer. In the nineteen-fifties Cuban architects and planners take the proposal up again and put the civic centre exactly where he put it. It becomes the Plaza Civica Jose Marti, and after 1959 the Plaza de la Revolucion.

stops.name: Paris, Officer of the Legion of Honour
stops.date_confidence: both 1926 honours are attested by es.wikipedia; month and day unknown, defaulted; Base Leonore holds a Legion d'honneur file under his name but only the search-results page title was retrievable, so its contents are unread
stops.campa: He is made an Officer of the Legion of Honour, and Spain names him Commander of the Order of Civil Merit in the same year. He is sixty-five, has never headed the service that employs him, and has built almost nothing of his own design in Paris; the works the two states are decorating stand in Seville, Barcelona, Buenos Aires and Havana. Leonore, the French state's register of the decorated, holds a file under his name. It could not be opened from here, so what his citation says goes unread.

stops.name: Lisbon, six days for an avenue
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia dates the Lisbon consultation 1927; the February date, the six-day stay, and the avenue dimensions come from the dossier's account of the Ville de Lisbonne study
stops.campa: The Lisbon Camara Municipal invites him in February and he stays about six days, the shortest commission of his life. In that time he proposes extending the Avenida da Liberdade as a planted avenue a hundred and fifty to two hundred metres wide, climbing to a great terraced park above the city with the Tagus in view from its head. What Lisbon eventually builds is broadly this, though not from his drawings and not soon. The park at the head of the avenue is Parque Eduardo VII.

stops.name: Bastide du Roy, Antibes: the theatre cut in cypress
stops.date_confidence: fr.wikipedia 'Bastide du Roy' gives 1927-1929, the commune as Antibes, and the patrons as the count and countess Jean de Polignac; en.wikipedia contradicts it on all three, giving Biot and the Princess of Polignac, and the contradiction is left standing; month defaulted
stops.campa: For the Comte and Comtesse Jean de Polignac, with the architect Louis Sue restoring the house, he lays out the garden of the Bastide du Roy: a theatre cut in cypress, a Spanish garden, a garden of santolina, all set inside olive and orange groves already standing on the ground. He works there until 1929. English reference gives the patron as the Princess of Polignac and puts the property at Biot; the French record gives the count and countess, and Antibes. Both are in print.

stops.name: Barcelona, the exhibition that finally opens
stops.date_confidence: the Grand Prize at the Barcelona International Exhibition is attested by es.wikipedia without a day; the date used is the exhibition's opening; the Seville exposition of the same year is attested separately
stops.campa: The exhibition he was called to Montjuic for in 1915 opens at last, fourteen years and one world war late, and the hill he terraced carries the German Pavilion, the Spanish Village, and the crowds. He is awarded a Grand Prize. In Seville the same year the Ibero-American Exposition opens in the park he began in 1911, eighteen years earlier, for a fair that had been postponed by a war nobody in 1911 expected. Two Spanish cities spend 1929 showing the world gardens he laid out before it. He is sixty-eight and lives in Paris.

stops.name: Villa Berriots, Ustaritz: the garden that outlives him
stops.date_confidence: the dossier dates the project 1929-1932, continuing after his death; this replaces the common claim that the Bastide du Roy was his final work, since that garden was finished in 1929; month defaulted
stops.campa: For the couturier Jean Patou he begins the garden of the Villa Berriots at Ustaritz in the Basque country, again with Louis Sue's team. The project is dated 1929 to 1932, on the authority of a single account that gives the years and little else. It is the last garden he begins, and the common claim that the Bastide du Roy was his final work is wrong on the dates: that garden was finished in 1929. He does not live to see Ustaritz done. The work goes on after his death, carried by other hands to a drawing already made.

stops.name: Paris, death at sixty-nine
stops.date_confidence: attested by en.wikipedia and corroborated by es.wikipedia; several accounts report a death following an operation, but no source located names the illness or the hospital, and no burial place has been found anywhere
stops.campa: He dies in Paris on the twenty-sixth of October, at sixty-nine. Several accounts say the death followed an operation; not one of them names the illness or the hospital. He had spent forty years in the employ of the City of Paris and had built his largest works in Seville, Barcelona, Buenos Aires, and Havana. A garden at Ustaritz is unfinished on his drawing board, and the Havana civic centre he proposed will not be built for another twenty-five years. Nine years later Jean Giraudoux, writing about what France owes its own cities, keeps one sentence of his.
stops.quote: Je suis un vrai homme des villes. J'aime l'air libre et les jardins.
stops.quote_source: Jean Giraudoux, Pleins pouvoirs (Paris, 1939), quoting Forestier; seen as reproduced on fr.wikipedia, the 1939 Gallimard edition not accessible
suggested_refs: Jean Giraudoux, Pleins pouvoirs, Paris 1939

stops.name: Paris, the grave no record names
stops.date_confidence: the date is arbitrary and orders the segment; the substance is a gap, not an event: the Cite de l'architecture's biography gives no burial information and no cemetery, tomb, plot, or probate record was located in any source reachable in this pass
stops.campa: Where he is buried is recorded nowhere that can be reached. The Cite de l'architecture's biography, the fullest institutional account of him there is, names no cemetery, no tomb, no plot. No burial register, no probate record and no monument has turned up in any source available here. A man who spent his working life persuading cities to secure ground for the public has no known ground of his own. Whether the grave is lost or merely unsearched is not something the record settles.

stops.name: Parque de Maria Luisa, the figure cut in the cypress
stops.date_confidence: the statue's existence is attested by two independent sources, sevillacitycentre.com and en.wikipedia's Forestier article, but no date for the carving was established; the year here is arbitrary and orders the segment only
stops.campa: In the Parque de Maria Luisa, behind the Mudejar Pavilion and beside the mound called Monte Gurugu, a figure is cut into the trunk of an old cypress in his honour. Not bronze, not on a plinth: a living tree carved where it stands, in the park he made, and it will last exactly as long as the tree does. Seville's official heritage copy names him as the French engineer who gave the park its character and says nothing about the statue. When it was carved has not been established.

stops.name: Rue Thomire, the garden that carries his name
stops.date_confidence: attested by paris.fr: 12 rue Thomire, Paris 13e, designed by Louis Benech, created 1994, with the coordinates given here taken from the same listing; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Paris gives his name to a garden at last, sixty-four years after his death: the Jardin Jean-Claude-Nicolas-Forestier at 12 rue Thomire in the thirteenth arrondissement, near the Stade Charlety, designed in 1994 by the landscape architect Louis Benech. It is a small neighbourhood garden of the kind his book had put third in its hierarchy, below the great reserve and the suburban park. Forestier never saw the ground and had no hand in the plan. The city he served for forty years, and could rarely persuade, commemorates him with somebody else's garden.
